skill.name: cm
skill.description: CASS Memory System adds procedural memory for AI coding agents by turning past sessions into reusable rules, warnings, and task context.
skill.summary: Build persistent cross-agent coding memory from session history, feedback, and playbook rules.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown code fences and inline command names. Confirmed risks are limited to user-initiated remote installer execution, sudo-based system installation, optional non-loopback server exposure, and sensitive agent session log processing.

remediation.issue: Remote install script is piped directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the one-line curl-to-bash path with a download, checksum verification, and local review step before execution.

remediation.issue: Source installation uses sudo to place a binary in /usr/local/bin.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a user-local install directory and document why elevated privileges are needed for system-wide installation.

remediation.issue: The tool processes raw AI agent session logs that may contain sensitive content.
remediation.suggestion: Make consent, redaction, retention limits, and opt-out behavior explicit before importing or reflecting on session logs.

remediation.issue: The MCP server example can bind to all network interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Keep loopback binding as the default and document firewall, token strength, and threat model requirements for non-loopback access.

content.value_statement: AI coding agents lose useful lessons when sessions end. CM turns past work into reusable rules, warnings, and context for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Retrieves task-specific playbook rules before coding work starts.
Tracks helpful and harmful feedback on stored coding rules.
Reflects on past sessions to create procedural memory entries.
Supports project and user-level memory storage locations.
Provides MCP tools and resources for agent integration.
Includes trauma guard patterns for blocking known dangerous commands.
limitations: Requires the separate CM or CASS command-line tooling to be installed.
May process sensitive session logs if users enable history-based reflection.
LLM-backed reflection requires provider API keys unless disabled.
The skill file is documentation-heavy and does not include implementation source code.

use_cases.title: Reuse lessons across coding agents
use_cases.description: Share successful debugging and architecture patterns between Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other agents.
use_cases.target_user: Senior engineers using multiple AI coding tools

use_cases.title: Create team playbooks from real sessions
use_cases.description: Turn repeated project decisions and fixes into rules that future agent sessions can retrieve.

use_cases.title: Warn agents about past mistakes
use_cases.description: Store harmful patterns and trauma guard rules so agents avoid repeating risky commands or bad approaches.

prompt_templates.title: Get task context
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup before a coding task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use CM to get relevant rules for this task: fix the login timeout bug.

prompt_templates.title: Review stored rules
prompt_templates.prompt: List the most relevant CM playbook rules for React testing and explain which ones apply today.

prompt_templates.title: Record feedback after work
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve rule quality after using memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Mark the rule about mocking modules as harmful for this session because it caused a regression.

prompt_templates.title: Build a safer team workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze recent sessions, identify repeated security mistakes, and propose CM trauma guard patterns for the project.

output_examples.input: Get context for fixing an authentication timeout.
output_examples.output: CM returns relevant rules about token expiry, past auth fixes, anti-pattern warnings, and suggested session searches.

output_examples.input: Reflect on the last seven days of coding sessions.
output_examples.output: CM summarizes repeated lessons, proposes new playbook entries, and flags weak rules that need validation.

output_examples.input: Check safety guard status before running risky commands.
output_examples.output: CM reports active trauma patterns, installed hooks, and commands that would be blocked or require review.

best_practices: Run context retrieval before non-trivial tasks and keep result limits small.
Review session privacy settings before enabling cross-agent enrichment.
Mark rules helpful or harmful so confidence scores stay accurate.
anti_patterns: Do not import sensitive session logs without consent and redaction review.
Do not treat generated rules as permanent without feedback validation.
Do not expose the MCP server beyond localhost without strong authentication.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It documents a memory workflow that turns AI coding sessions into reusable rules, history, and safety warnings.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is positioned for Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and other coding agents that can call the CM CLI or MCP server.

faq.question: Does it require cloud sync?
faq.answer: The documentation describes a local-first design with no cloud sync and optional cross-agent enrichment.

faq.question: Can it work without LLM calls?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes an LLM-free mode for deterministic behavior, though semantic reflection is reduced.

faq.question: What data does it process?
faq.answer: It can process playbooks, outcomes, trauma patterns, and agent session logs stored on the user machine.

faq.question: What should users review before installing?
faq.answer: Users should review the remote installer, sudo installation step, privacy settings, and any non-local MCP server configuration.
